doc.title: Eddie Miller and Pete Fountain Interview, 1970-01-09

title: Lawrence Welk days and red beans and rice
summary: A caller recalls Pete with Lawrence Welk; Pete says he returned for red beans and rice, and callers compare beans.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I was thinking about when Pete was with Lawrence Welk. A lady next door used to say to me to come in on Saturday night, and we would sit with her husband and watch the Lawrence Welk show. It was such a clean show that I didn't mind watching it. And the one tickle me, Pete said he had to come back to New Orleans to get his red beans and rice.

I don't know whether it's the water or what it is, but you just can't, they just don't have the same taste out there, the red beans. We used to get them sent out, and they call them a different kind of bean out there. Yeah. Uh-huh. It's not the red, but my wife, Beverly, we would try to cook them, but I think it's just the atmosphere in New Orleans, too, that the red beans stays good. You know, uh... With the French bread.
I see them from the north, and we used to buy red beans, just red beans. And here in New Orleans, all I can find is red kidney beans.
The difference, you know, between the red beans and the red kidney beans.

Right. Well, in California, we'd get the red beans, and we were looking for the kidney beans. Got it. Just like you looking for the kidney beans on, I mean the red beans, and you're getting the kidney beans. Yeah. Well, well, well, I'm all mixed up. Excuse me.
I like the red beans, and I don't really... This is not the red kidney. They're so large or something.
And I just like the red beans, but for now, I have never seen a bag. I've been here almost 15 years now, and I've never seen red beans. It's always red kidney beans.
Yeah. Well, thank you for calling.
